_universal.hours_sim: open 18:00 ET Sun-Thu; all positions AUTO-FLATTENED 16:45 ET Mon-Fri; holiday closes override the usual cutoff. Holding past the cutoff does NOT fail the account.
_universal.hours_live: 16:45 ET Tradovate Live / 16:15 ET Rithmic Live; swing trading prohibited
_universal.news_restriction: allowed without restriction in every phase — no lockout window, no size reduction around scheduled news

activity_requirement.threshold: at least one trade producing >= $1 net profit or loss
activity_requirement.consequence: account deemed abandoned and PERMANENTLY DELETED
activity_requirement.weekly_requirement: none — Lucid has NO weekly round-trip requirement, unlike Take Profit Trader
activity_requirement.note: Separately, breached evaluations are auto-deleted 30 days after the breach if not reset; they stay resettable inside that window.

account_death_conditions: MLL breach — account breached (see _gaps.breach_basis for the open question on WHEN this is evaluated)

INACTIVITY: any account with no trade producing >= $1 net profit or loss within 30 CALENDAR days is deemed abandoned and PERMANENTLY DELETED. Applies to evals and funded accounts alike. No weekly activity requirement exists.
Breached evaluations are auto-deleted after 30 days if not reset (they remain resettable inside that window)

Moving to live CLOSES ALL remaining simulated accounts, including untouched evals held in reserve — Lucid warns explicitly: 'If you are not comfortable with evaluations being closed, do not keep evaluations in reserve'
HOUSEHOLD LIVE RULE: once one household member trades live, no other member may trade sim at all
Repeated hedging, HFT or microscalping offenses: profit forfeiture, account closure, permanent ban
2-week cooldown after blowing a live account bars new evaluation purchases during that window (longer at risk-team discretion for reckless behavior)

prohibited.hedging: all forms — cross-account, cross-user, cross-firm, and CORRELATED instruments in separate accounts (long ES + short NQ = violation). Long mini + short micro of the SAME contract WITHIN ONE account is allowed. 1st offense: accounts reset to prior-day balance. Repeat: breach + permanent ban. Live hedging = immediate permanent ban.
prohibited.hft: warning first, then all HFT profits removed + accounts closed + permanent ban. Appealable.
prohibited.microscalping: flagged when >50% of profits come from trades held <= 5 seconds. Manual review, then warning, then profit forfeiture and possible permanent ban. Appealable.
prohibited.other: exploiting system errors or update delays, exploiting simulated-price discrepancies, tactics not reflecting real-world trading

permitted: DCA / scaling into positions (martingale discouraged but not banned)
automated strategies and trade copiers (trader owns all software failures)
flipping — quick in-and-out trades purely to satisfy day counts, explicitly not restricted

max_accounts.note: 5 evals may be held in reserve alongside 5 funded accounts, and reserve evals may be traded — but they are all closed on the move to live

_universal.payout_processing: no fixed payout window; request any day once criteria are met. Deducted from the account within minutes of approval; disbursed within 2 business days. Requests are FINAL once submitted — cannot be edited or cancelled. Trading after submitting but before approval that drops the balance below the required level can get the request denied.
payout_methods: WorkMarket by ADP (US + international, bank or PayPal, often next business day)

breach_basis.status: UNVERIFIED — the highest-impact open question in this file
breach_basis.why: Lucid's documentation uses the word 'balance' in every single instance and NEVER uses 'equity' or 'unrealized'. A help-center search for 'unrealized' returns ZERO articles. The trailing (hwm_basis) is unambiguously end-of-day close. But no primary page states whether an open losing position that dips below the MLL mid-session breaches the account immediately.
breach_basis.evidence_for_close_only: The LucidMaxx cooldown article says 'If trading activity causes drawdown to EXCEED the defined Max Loss Limit...' — drawdown being able to exceed the MLL implies no instantaneous hard stop-out at that level. Secondary reviews state 'intraday swings that would blow you up at other firms are survivable as long as you recover by the close.'
breach_basis.evidence_for_intraday: The DLL article's phrase 'provided your account has not been liquidated' implies a real-time liquidation engine exists. Rithmic/CQG typically enforce risk limits in real time.
breach_basis.impact: Binary. Changes survival probability materially in any Monte Carlo. This is the field where Lucid may diverge from the other four firms — do NOT default it to intraday_equity_incl_unrealized just because Topstep/MFF/TPT do.
breach_basis.how_to_close: Ask Lucid support verbatim: 'If my open position takes my equity below the MLL mid-session but I close green before 16:45 ET, is the account breached?' Or buy a $100 LucidFlex 25K eval and observe.

profit_target_basis.why: Never stated whether the target counts unrealized P&L at the moment it is touched, or only closed balance. Same 'balance'-only vocabulary as above.

dll_basis.status: UNVERIFIED for every row that has a DLL
dll_basis.why: Realized vs unrealized never specified. Note the DLL is a SOFT breach everywhere at Lucid — hitting it locks trading until the next session but does not kill the account, so the blast radius of getting this wrong is smaller than breach_basis.

dll_reset_time.why: Docs say only 'until the next trading session'. The 18:00 ET session open is documented separately, so 18:00 ET is a strong inference — but it is an inference, flagged inline on every affected node.

profit_split_live.why: 90/10 is stated for funded-sim and explicitly for LucidMaxx live, but the LucidLive articles never restate it. The homepage lists '90/10 Profit Split' under Step 2 (sim funded), not Step 3 (live). Real-capital split may differ. DO NOT assume 90%.
profit_split_live.how_to_close: Support ticket, or the LucidLive onboarding docs which are not public.

min_payout_and_max_withdrawal_live.why: 'Daily payouts' only; no floor or cap published. LucidMaxx is explicitly uncapped; standard live is silent.

lucidmaxx_max_contracts_and_dd_lock.why: The LucidMaxx eval table omits both columns entirely. Live drawdown is stated to match the standard live structure, but the eval-phase contract cap and trail balance are never given.

lucidblack_pricing.why: Product sunset; pricing removed from the site. Both account_cost and reset_cost are unavailable for eval and funded.

luciddirect_reset_cost_and_buffer.why: The pricing card shows no reset fee and the fees article scopes resets to EVALUATIONS only — whether a breached LucidDirect can be reset at all is unstated. Separately: Pro documents a buffer, Flex and Black explicitly say 'none', Direct is SILENT. Silence is not 'none' — left null.

luciddirect_min_days_conflict.why: lucidtrading.com pricing card: 'Min Day to Payout: 5' on every size. support.lucidtrading.com payout article: only two criteria listed, no day requirement. Both are Lucid properties. Took the more restrictive value, which is also the one shown at checkout.

luciddirect_100k_legacy_live.why: Lucid's own legacy move-to-live table for LucidDirect lists 25K/50K/150K only. The 100K row simply does not exist in their documentation.

secondary_claims_rejected: 'LucidPro has 3-day payout cycles' — asserted by several review sites; ABSENT from Lucid's own payout article, which lists exactly three criteria (min profit goal, 40% consistency, profit over buffer). Primary wins: min_days recorded as 0.
'Minimum trading days are low (e.g. two days)' for LucidFlex — treated as an arithmetic consequence of the 50% consistency rule, not as a stated rule.
